meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Unitary state; no separate sub-state taxing jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French Napoleonic tradition) with strong European Union legal harmonization; unitary national legal system without sub-state tax distinctions.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal legal framework is: (i) the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, governing the SARL; (ii) the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, implementing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; (iii) the amended Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), integrated into the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); (iv) the Law of 19 December 2020 on financial sanctions; and (v) Grand-Ducal implementing regulations and CSSF AML/CFT circulars. For pre-incorporation, all ultimate beneficial owners must be identified, verified and comprehensively profiled before the Luxembourg notary signs the deed of incorporation, and the RBE filing must be made immediately upon registration of the SARL.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (competent authorities and statutorily authorized AML/CFT obliged entities with legitimate-interest access; not general-public access following the CJEU limitation on unrestricted UBO publication)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, signatories and beneficial owners against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the consolidated EU financial sanctions list and EU restrictive measures database; (iii) the U.S. Department of the Treasury OFAC SDN List and other OFAC sanctions programs where US dollar clearing or US persons are involved; (iv) Luxembourg financial sanctions implemented under the Law of 19 December 2020 on financial sanctions; and (v) domestic and international law-enforcement adverse media and Politically Exposed Person (PEP) indicators. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign and domestic PEPs, their close family members and close associates, and for high-risk third-country relationships. Screening results and underlying KYC evidence must be documented in a written compliance file retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registers of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), online portal www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be composed in French, German, English, Luxembourgish or another language using Latin script. If a non-Latin alphabet is used, the RCS requires a Latin-script transliteration of the name. The name must be distinctive, non-misleading, and compliant with Luxembourg public order. In all corporate communications and on the RCS registration, the name must be followed by or accompanied by the legal-form identifier 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or its abbreviation 'SARL'. Names suggesting a link to the Luxembourg State, the Crown, the Grand-Ducal family, the European Union or public institutions require prior ministerial or administrative authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The notary or incorporation counsel will first obtain a written availability/name-clearance statement from the Luxembourg Business Registers. If the proposed name is rejected, the procedure is: (i) request written reasons from LBR within 15 days of refusal; (ii) file a reconsideration request with the LBR registrar, including any correcting explanation or a modified name; (iii) if the refusal is confirmed, lodge an administrative appeal before the Tribunal administratif within two months of notification, or, where the refusal is treated as a private-right issue, an action before the Civil Chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg; and (iv) concurrently reserve two alternative cleared names so the notarial deed may be executed without loss of transactional timing. A reserved name may be extended at the registrar's discretion by filing an extension request before expiry; otherwise the name-clearance expires after 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only in the form of a professional domiciliation arrangement with a qualified corporate-service provider maintaining a physical Luxembourg address where legal notices can be served and the governing-body authorized representatives can be contacted. A mere post-office box or non-physical virtual address is not acceptable for RCS registration. For a fully digital royalty-free stock-music licensing marketplace, a professional domiciliation address is acceptable if complemented by real commercial substance: a Luxembourg bank or EMI account, board minutes taken in Luxembourg, contracting counterparty records, and a responsible management function effectively exercised in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10-15% unannounced physical inspection probability in the first three fiscal years for a low-risk online audio-licensing SARL. If the SARL files large VAT refund claims, reports sustained tax losses, requests a tax ruling or applies for state-aid benefit, the likelihood of an announced or unannounced inspection rises to approximately 30%. Social-security and business-permit inspections of a registered-office-only structure are rare but possible where the domiciliation provider is audited by Luxembourg authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended by the Law of 23 September 2020 on the modernisation of the SARL; Articles 710-1, 710-2, 710-4, 710-9, 710-16 and 710-18 (minimum capital, incorporation deed, shares, and management).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 3 Avenue du Swing, L-4368 Belvaux, Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) executed by a Luxembourg notary and registered by deposit with the RCS; publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up before incorporation; cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked special account (compte bloqué) opened in Luxembourg in the name of the company being formed and blocked until the deed is signed and the RCS registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the sole incorporator approves in full the subscription of the EUR 12,000 share capital, comprising 12,000 fully paid shares of EUR 1.00 each, as set out in the deed of incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office is fixed at [Registered Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, until relocated by a duly adopted shareholders' resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with unlimited sole signatory authority, and [Name] is appointed alternate Manager. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Manager is authorized to open bank accounts, complete RCS and RESA filings, obtain VAT and administrative identifiers, and execute all ancillary corporate formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) RCS online counter (https://www.lbr.lu) and notary's pre-verification via the Ministry of Economy nomenclature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed legal names for the SARL via the RCS name check; the selected name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade mark or company, must not contravene Luxembourg public policy, and must be compatible with the structure (Société à Responsabilité Limitée or SARL). A notary or certified authorized agent files the reservation form electronically; the RCS issues a name availability certificate valid for 2 months.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or ID of the shareholder
Proof of identity of future Manager
Proof of registered business address (lease agreement or usufruct consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new application with a distinct denominative element and provide a reasoned submission; appeal to the administrative court within 3 months if refusal is arbitrary.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg — Service de la TVA (VAT registration, OSS filings and indirect tax audits), portal: MyGuichet.lu / eTVA (https://myguichet.lu, https://pfi.public.lu); direct tax competence: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu; customs competence: Administration des douanes et accises (https://douanes.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Resident SARL: incorporation filing at the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu triggers attribution of the 13-digit national business number (matricule), which serves as the national TIN and as the basis for the Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + matricule). Non-resident foreign supplier: file the AEDT non-established taxable person VAT registration request (digital 'VAT identification' form published by the AEDT via the PFI/eTVA portal), attaching a certified copy of the foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutive documents, proof of identity and authority of the legal representative, foreign VAT ID (for EU suppliers), NACE/ISIC description of the audio-licensing activity, evidence of any Luxembourg fixed establishment, and bank details; the AEDT then issues a Luxembourg VAT number. Digital-services suppliers may alternatively submit a Union/Non-Union OSS registration through the national OSS portal for B2C intra-EU electronic supplies. VAT registration is mandatory before issuing compliant invoices and claiming input VAT deduction under section 25 of the Luxembourg VAT Law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Luxembourg; the SARL is an opaque, fully taxable company subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax. Available elections relevant to cross-border structures: (i) fiscal unity election (intégration fiscale) under section 164bis LIR for resident companies held directly or indirectly at not less than 95%; (ii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under section 25a of the VAT Law; (iii) IP box election under section 50bis LIR granting an 80% exemption on qualifying digital/audio royalty income; (iv) small-trader franchise option under section 28 VAT Law below the EUR 35,000 turnover threshold; (v) OSS/Union scheme election for distance sales and electronically supplied services; (vi) hybrid mismatch rules are applied statutorily under ATAD (section 168quater LIR) with no elective carve-out for hybrid instruments or payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), EU VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual national taxable turnover for the small-trader franchise exemption, section 28 VAT Law); EUR 10,000 (Union-wide annual turnover of intra-EU distance sales and electronically supplied services to non-taxable persons, above which destination-country VAT applies via OSS or local registration, section 58(2) VAT Law)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G: mandatory e-invoicing since 1 January 2024 for invoices addressed to Luxembourg public authorities (Peppol network, EN 16931, Factur-X/UBL format). B2B: e-invoicing remains voluntary; no national real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, QR code or daily electronic transaction transfer obligation applies to commercial audio-licensing invoices. Tax control is enforced through periodic e-filed VAT returns (monthly/quarterly/annual) on MyGuichet/eTVA, the AEDT's standard-audit-file inspection practice, and 10-year record-retention duties. EU ViDA real-time digital reporting and a general EN 16931 e-invoicing mandate are expected from approximately 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: dispatch of physical merchandise from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations qualifies for the 0% rate when the electronic export declaration (IE-599/SAD) is accepted by the Administration des douanes et accises and transport evidence is retained within the statutory 90-day proof window. Digital services (royalty-free stock-music licensing and subscriptions): supplies are classified as electronically supplied services (ESS). B2B supplies to customers established outside Luxembourg are zero-rated/outside Luxembourg VAT (place of supply at the customer's establishment; foreign customer VAT ID or residence certificate required). B2C supplies to consumers outside the EU are outside Luxembourg VAT. B2C supplies to EU consumers exceeding EUR 10,000 Union-wide are taxable in the destination Member State through the OSS rather than Luxembourg zero-rating; supplies below that threshold remain taxable at Luxembourg rates unless the destination-state option is elected.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (IE-599 / Single Administrative Document) cleared by the Luxembourg Administration des douanes et accises
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch from Luxembourg to a non-EU country
Commercial invoice and executed licence/subscription agreement describing the royalty-free music exploitation rights and consideration
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank credit advice evidencing settlement of the foreign sales proceeds
Foreign customer's valid VAT identification number or certificate of residence establishing B2B status for place-of-supply purposes
OSS quarterly returns and transaction-level digital records where B2C electronic supplies to EU consumers are reported
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retroactively review VAT positions for 5 years, extended to 10 years where concealment or fraud is established. Unsupported export zero-rating is clawed back by reassessment at the domestic Luxembourg VAT rate (currently 17%) together with monthly statutory late-payment interest and administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 per taxpayer per infringement. Willful electronic-service VAT evasion is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and court-imposed fines; fraudulent OSS declarations can trigger joint liability for VAT of all destination Member States, exclusion from the OSS regime, and compulsory posting of security.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism; prudential supervision of banks is shared with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies no exchange controls. The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Profit remittances are unrestricted under Luxembourg and EU capital movement rules, subject only to ordinary corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and, where applicable, withholding tax obligations. No prior administrative approval is required for dividend distributions, loan repayments, or royalty outbound payments, provided that AML/KYC reporting thresholds and BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting are satisfied. The Luxembourg entity operates in EUR; settlement of USD or other foreign-currency licensing receipts is freely permitted and may be retained in foreign currency or converted without restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds or foreign-currency receipts. The SARL may retain offshore or onshore funds in any currency, subject to corporate substance, transfer pricing, and controlled-foreign-corporation considerations arising under the tax law of the foreign revenue jurisdiction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited-Low as primary treasury rail; Medium-Only as a receivable collection channel. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) proceeding under PSD2 and CSSF supervision may provide multicurrency virtual IBANs and low-cost cross-border collection, but they are not full credit institutions and cannot support capital escrow arrangements, commercial letters of credit, or material FX derivative negotiations. Unregulated foreign EMIs, including non-Luxembourg PSPs such as Stripe and PayPal, are acceptable only for marketplace collections, not as sole treasury counterparties; all major liquidity and hedging operations must be conducted through a BCL-supervised credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorised director, or a duly mandated Luxembourg-resident notarized attorney-in-fact, is generally required for initial corporate account opening under the Luxembourg AML/CFT framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF regulations). Some banks allow remote video identification for directors resident in recognised high-AML-standard jurisdictions, but this remains discretionary and is normally rejected for non-EU directors unless a physical intro call at the bank’s registration office is made. Documents must bear apostille or legalisation where relevant, and the registered office lease and beneficial owner declaration must be verifiable before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: undisclosed or multi-layer non-EU holding structures above the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association; complete corporate chain charts; certified shareholders register; excerpt from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); passport copies; valid residence/business address proof for each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth and initial capital injection: inability to evidence lawful origin of equity capital or shareholder loan funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital contribution or share subscription deed; bank reference or source-of-funds documentary trail (tax returns, asset disposition statements, inheritance/gift instruments, audited financial statements of the investing shareholder); confirmation that the minimum €12,500 SARL share capital requirement has been fully subscribed and paid.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online marketplace revenue profile: high-volume low-value royalty collections via Stripe/PayPal raising concerns over unauthorised licensing or unverified counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete license agreements with end customers; the B2B marketplace seller verification records; periodic payout statements from PSPs showing settlement to the SARL account; royalty computation methodology; audited or management-prepared financial statements demonstrating coherent business substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening flags on shareholders, signatories, or counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative news and OCC/SIP-screening certificates dated within 30 days; identity and nationality documentation; supporting résumé/business reference confirming absence of adverse histories; written confirmation of no public office for each director/UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin substance in Luxembourg: no payroll, physical office, or local decision-making evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease agreement; tax and social-security filings; management accounts reviewed by a Luxembourg certified accountant; employment contracts or management agreements for Luxembourg-resident directors/managers; annual general meeting minutes and board resolutions prepared in Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: route initial share capital and subsequent capital increases by SWIFT MT103 (non-EEA remitter) or SEPA Credit Transfer (EEA remitter) using the SARL’s Luxembourg IBAN at the onboarding bank. The payment must include the beneficiary legal name exactly matching the KYC profile, the corporate registration number RCS, and a purpose code falling within BCL balance-of-payments nomenclature for direct investment/capital participation; acceptable descriptors include 'CAPT' or 'INVS' (capital injection/investment). The bank will require the notarized deed of incorporation or capital-increase resolution before accepting the wire. For amounts above €10,000 or any risk-sensitive jurisdiction, source-of-funds evidence must be pre-submitted. After settlement, verification is completed by reconciling the bank credit advice with the notarial certificate, registering the capital increase with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and updating the RBE register if ownership changed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty and licensing disbursements from the SARL to foreign music copyright owners, distributors, or co-licensors settle primarily through SWIFT MT103 covered transfers, with field 72 purpose code reflecting 'ROYL' (royalty/license fee) or 'INTC' (intra-group services) where applicable. Within the eurozone, low-value disbursements (<€100,000) can use SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or standard SEPA CT; outside the EEA, a conventional SWIFT EUR/USD payment is mandatory. For high-value contractual trade settlements requiring documentary protection, a Commercial Letter of Credit (import/export LC) or documentary collection against presentation of licence acceptance certificates and delivery confirmations is the appropriate clearing rail. All outbound payments must be screened against EU/UN sanctions lists; payments to restricted jurisdictions may be rejected or referred for OFAC/ECOFIN regulatory analysis. The bank will also require BCL balance-of-payments reporting classification for each outbound transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forward contracts concluded with an EEA/Luxembourg-authorised credit institution under an ISDA Master Agreement or bank FX line documentation
EUR/USD FX swaps for short-term matching of USD licensing receipts against EUR operating expenditures
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for longer-dated contracted royalty streams or intercompany funding commitments
Vanilla FX options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) permitted for hedging committed forecast licensing revenues, subject to bank counterparty policy

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) are legally permissible under Luxembourg law but operationally unnecessary and generally unavailable because EUR/USD is a fully convertible deliverable pair; banks will normally decline NDF execution absent a genuine offshore-deliverability constraint

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss account and notes, deposited with the Luxembourg trade register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; a calendar-year SARL must deposit by 31 July of the following year and only after shareholders' approval of the accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On petition of the Public Prosecutor, the President of the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg may impose coercive fines for each month of delay; absence of filed accounts for 3 consecutive financial years exposes the SARL to judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner information (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the anniversary of the initial RBE registration in each calendar year; the confirmation duty persists even when beneficial ownership is unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Admin fines up to EUR 125,000 (approx. USD 135,000) for the SARL and up to EUR 25,000 per officer; criminal sanctions including imprisonment for intentionally false declarations; sanctions may be published by the RBE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct-tax return covering corporate income tax (CIS), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., FY 2024 return due 31 December 2025); the ACD may grant filing extensions up to 31 March or 30 June of the subsequent year under its e-file practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to EUR 5,000 (approx. USD 5,400) under the Luxembourg General Tax Code; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; ex-officio assessment and enforced collection proceedings that may culminate in tax-distress sale and administrative deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders approving the annual accounts and granting discharge to the managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory records (shareholders' minute book); approved accounts subsequently filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held within 6 months of financial year-end (calendar-year SARL: by 30 June); accounts must be approved prior to the 31 July RCS filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers face civil liability for failure to table accounts; the District Court may impose coercive fines; omission for 3 consecutive fiscal years supports the Public Prosecutor's petition for judicial dissolution and strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit by an independent Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé is mandatory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds of the Law of 19 December 2002 for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance-sheet total over EUR 4.4 million; (ii) net turnover over EUR 8.8 million; (iii) average headcount over 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP per the Law of 19 December 2002 (Plan Comptable Normalisé); EU-endorsed IFRS is permissible and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups; statutory accounts are drawn up in EUR in French, German or Luxembourgish, or in English with a certified translation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law of 13 January 2019 (art. 23): the SARL must confirm annually, within 1 month of the anniversary of its initial RBE filing, that recorded beneficial-owner data are accurate; any share transfer or change in ultimate ownership must be declared to the RBE within 1 month of the change and cannot be postponed to the next annual confirmation; confirmation is submitted electronically via the RBE e-space free of charge.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des parts sociales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,900 - 3,800 per annum (EUR 1,750 - 3,500) for a Luxembourg registered office / domiciliation agent including routine RCS, RBE and secretarial handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,800 - 27,000 (EUR 10,000 - 25,000) for a certified statutory audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé; nil while the SARL remains below the statutory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate in Luxembourg City: 17% national corporate income tax, plus 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, plus municipal business tax of 6.75%; municipal rate varies by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to stock-music licensing. Luxembourg IP box regime exempts 80% of qualifying net IP income, mainly patents and qualifying copyrighted software; Luxembourg City effective rate on qualifying IP is approximately 4.99%. A catalog of royalty-free stock music and sound-recording licensing rights is generally not qualifying IP unless separately protected software is involved. Participation exemption is available for qualifying dividends and capital gains.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_comment: Luxembourg allows indefinite carryforward of tax losses under LIR Article 114; no carryback is permitted. The 9999 encoding denotes unlimited carryforward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 705 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / eCDF portal of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; quarterly CIT advance-payment instalments are assessed and collected by ACD on the basis of the preceding year's tax assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a tax year ending on 31 December, the return is due by 31 December of the following calendar year unless ACD notifies a different filing date or an extension is granted. E-filing is mandatory for companies; non-receipt of a pre-printed form does not discharge the filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS Luxembourg number, matricule number, registered office, legal form SARL, and identification of the appointed manager/director.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL itself is the taxpayer; use the Luxembourg RCS and matricule. A non-resident manager may be identified, but no foreign tax identification number is accepted as the Luxembourg taxpayer reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period, currency, and duration of the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-calendar accounting periods must be reflected exactly; loss carryforward and proration are calculated for that precise period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss per the annual accounts (compte de profits et pertes), after commercial-law adjustments and before tax deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This field captures Luxembourg-resident SARL income only. Income belonging to non-resident shareholders is not entered in Form 705 and is not taxable as Luxembourg corporate income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of net income from qualifying IP benefiting from the 80% exemption, derived from qualifying patents and copyrighted software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalty-free stock-music catalog revenue is normally not qualifying IP; the schedule should not be used for ordinary sound-recording licensing income. Over-qualification is an audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses available from prior years and the amount set off against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg losses may be carried forward indefinitely but are subject to anti-abuse limitations on a change of business. Losses of the SARL may not be used by a non-resident shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions, counterparties, transaction values, and transfer-pricing methodology.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL must report transactions with non-resident affiliates even when treaty relief is claimed; documentary proof should be contemporaneous.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing permits ACD to issue a default assessment. Civil penalties under Luxembourg General Tax Law generally range from EUR 25 to EUR 2,500 for negligent non-compliance, plus monthly late-payment interest on the unpaid tax at the current ACD rate. Deliberate non-filing may trigger criminal tax treatment with harsher fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on Luxembourg-source dividends. Rate is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where a qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholder holds at least 10% and meets substance/anti-abuse conditions; applicable DTA often reduces the rate to 5% for substantial holdings and 15% for portfolio dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain relief at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Luxembourg paying entity or paying agent with a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty state, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and, where applicable, Luxembourg Form 105 or the equivalent ACD residence certificate. If relief is not granted at source, the shareholder may file a refund claim with the Luxembourg direct tax administration, attaching the same TRC, dividend vouchers, and shareholding evidence. The SARL should also verify the participation exemption and confirm that the arrangement has genuine economic substance before applying reduced WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg statutory law imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest. Royalties and debt interest paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-resident beneficial owners are generally paid gross, subject to anti-abuse rules, the arm's-length principle, and the Luxembourg EU Interest and Royalties Directive implementation. Payments recharacterized as hidden dividend distributions can be reclassified as dividends and become subject to 15% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are triggered for Luxembourg members of MNE groups with consolidated group turnover of at least EUR 50,000,000 under Article 56bis LIR and OECD TP documentation standards. Below this threshold, the SARL must still produce contemporaneous evidence of arm's-length pricing when intercompany transactions exist, and the Controlled Transactions Annex to Form 705 must be completed where applicable.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no separately named Economic Substance Regulations, but the same substance principle is enforced through tax residence rules, Article 56bis LIR, EU ATAD GAAR, Luxembourg administrative circulars, and treaty-beneficial-ownership requirements. The SARL must maintain a registered office, active director decisions, employees or subcontracting substance, a Luxembourg bank account, and commercial activity. A mailbox-only structure with no real management of music-licensing contracts will be disregarded and denied treaty and participation-exemption benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting digital sales received through Stripe or PayPal, using undisclosed personal merchant accounts for corporate stock-music revenue, fabricating deductions, or filing a false Form 705 with ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD will apply reassessment of the full omitted income, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties. Criminal conviction under Luxembourg General Tax Law can lead to imprisonment of up to five years and substantial criminal fines commensurate with the evaded tax, in addition to full restitution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or manager who signs or directs the false return is the liable natural person. Criminal asset freezes, travel bans, and seizure of personal bank accounts may be ordered. In insolvency, the director may be ordered to contribute personally to the SARL's liabilities under Luxembourg company-law management-liability rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL with no office, no staff, no local bank account, and no real management activity, while using the SARL as a conduit to license stock-music rights and distribute profits offshore under treaty or participation-exemption protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD and tax courts may disregard the structure as abusive, deny the tax residence certificate, deny treaty and Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, reallocate income to the true owner or controlling shareholder, and treat previously exempt dividends and gains as fully taxable. Administrative penalties and default interest apply; the company may also be struck from the Luxembourg trade register for failure to maintain lawful corporate substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish or maintain an artificial shell may be held civilly liable for resulting tax losses, subject to court-ordered restitution and asset freezes. In serious cases involving intentional abuse, criminal fines and travel restrictions can be imposed on the responsible individuals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify and update the ultimate beneficial owner in the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), or allowing Stripe/PayPal-settled subscription and licensing payments to be routed through personal accounts to obscure the real economic beneficiary of the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to comply with RBE and AML/CFT filing obligations attracts criminal sanctions under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 and the RBE Law, including fines and imprisonment for natural persons. Administrative sanctions may be imposed separately on the SARL, and the authorities may enroll the company in a public non-compliance registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director, as the registered responsible officer, is personally exposed to criminal fines and imprisonment. Prosecutors may obtain freezing orders over the director's assets and prohibit departure from Luxembourg while an AML investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Violation / Abusive Royalty-Free Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concluding intercompany licensing contracts that charge zero or non-arm's-length royalties for the stock-music catalog, or aggregating all valuable sound-recording rights in a low-tax related entity without corresponding substance, functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 56bis LIR permits ACD to re-determine taxable income by applying the arm's-length principle and adjusting the SARL's profit upward. The adjustment may be accompanied by default interest, late-payment penalties, and, where the transaction is part of a fraudulent avoidance scheme, criminal tax penalties. Failure to produce TP documentation upon request is independently sanctionable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who approves biased intercompany transfer prices without supporting economic analysis can be jointly liable for the additional corporate taxes, interest, and penalties. In fraud-based adjustments, the director's personal assets may be subject to attachment and the individual may be barred from leaving Luxembourg during criminal proceedings.
